task: Review every supplied part, discover the most consequential events from the supplied evidence, cluster related reports, assign the best-fit broad news category dynamically and produce up to 150 processed stories using schema/processed-news.schema.json. More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.title: Not a dispute that should come before us: Supreme Court grants Mahua Moitra relief in accommodation row
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday modified a September 1 communication that required All India Trinamool Congress (TMC) Member of Parliament (MP) Mahua Moitra to give three to four days’ notice before staying at the Krishnanagar Circuit House in West Bengal. The Court said that she need only inform the district administration a day before her visit. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi passed the order while hearing Moitra’s plea alleging that she was asked to vacate the government guest house in the middle of the night on August 14, despite having been allotted a room. The Court said that the accommodation could be provided in accordance with protocol following advance intimation. It also directed that the September 1 communication be modified to that extent. “These are not issues which, in fact, should come to the Court. Probably what we require is only a small SOP,” CJI Kant remarked during the hearing. He suggested that a standard operating procedure (SOP) be put in place for allotment of government circuit houses and guest houses to MPs and other eligible public functionaries.
